passage: Sunday, late. I slipped this weekend. Saturday and most of Sunday went on videos, and I feel low about it. But I've decided not to be horrible to myself, because that never helped. Instead I asked what set it off. First there was the argument with my brother on Friday, which left me angry and restless. Then there was nothing planned, so the empty hours filled up. That's two triggers: a fight and boredom. So here's what changes: next Saturday I've asked my friend Keerthana to go to the market with me, something fixed and outside. And tomorrow I start again as normal. One bad weekend doesn't cancel the two good weeks. — Rekha

qa.q: What set off the weekend of videos?
qa.a: An argument with a brother and having nothing planned.

qa.q: How does Rekha feel about the slip, and how is it handled?
qa.a: Low and disappointed, but Rekha chooses to be kind to self instead of harsh, and looks for triggers.

qa.q: What else could Rekha do to prepare for boring stretches, and why?
qa.a: Keep a short list of things to do when bored, since a ready list is easier to use than deciding on the spot.

qa.q: How does the outing look to Keerthana?
qa.a: Keerthana, invited to the market, may feel glad to be included and to help a friend get through a hard weekend.

grounding: After a weekend slip, a student checks the triggers, plans an outing for next weekend and restarts the next day.
